front: pull the wool over the public's eyes
back: To deceive the public, often used by critics to describe modern art they believe is a trick [1].
An inability to appreciate art or culture (disapproving term) [1].
Critics who disagree with or speak ill of a particular work or movement [1].
To become more sophisticated or aware of something [1].
To become less intellectual, usually to appeal to a mass audience [1].
To show disapproval by stopping coming to an exhibition or event [1].
Being educated or knowledgeable with regard to art [1].
Not affected by something that might shock others [1].
Highbrow is for educated/intelligent people (often elitist); lowbrow is for a mass audience [1].
Inspiring great admiration because it is brilliant (opposite: pedestrian) [1].
Better than any other; without equal (opposite: run-of-the-mill) [1].
Not intended to be taken seriously despite appearing serious (opposite: earnest) [1].
